children: Algeria is progressing with project preparation works for the 495-kilometre (km) Laghouat-Ghardaïa-El Meniaa railway line in the county’s southern region, as authorities work to clear administrative and on-the-ground obstacles before construction begins, according to local Arabic language news portal Ennaharonline.

The report published on Monday said a joint interministerial committee chaired by Public Works and Basic Infrastructure Minister Abdelkader Djellaoui reviewed the project’s progress ahead of start of construction, including measures taken to remove constraints on Ouargla-El Menia and El Menia-Ain Salah-Tamanrasset sections.

African Development Bank (AfDB) is the key financier of the project, providing a €747.32 million ($866 million) loan for the 265-km first phase from Laghouat to Ghardaïa, and a $878.09 million loan for 230-km second phase from Ghardaïa to El Meniaa section, according to statements and data available on the bank’s website. Other financiers include the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) and the Government of Algeria.
The entire 495-km railway is estimated to cost approximately $2.93 billion, according to AfDB.

Once completed, the project is expected to boost agricultural and mining production in the provinces along the railway corridor by improving access to markets and reducing transport costs and travel times while stimulating economic activity in agro-industry, logistics, construction and public works sectors.

In addition, the project will strengthen regional integration along the planned Trans-Saharan railway corridor linking Algiers with Tamanrasset in the south, while enhancing the competitiveness of rail transport as an alternative to road freight.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: Algeria moves ahead with preparatory works for 495km railway project
